title: Credibility assessment of CFD models for vibrating mesh nebulizer droplet size distribution under ASME V&V 40
runhead: CFD credibility for vibrating mesh nebulizer
device: Vibrating mesh nebulizer intended to generate a therapeutic aerosol with targeted droplet size distribution

models.name: Mesh-Resolved Two-Phase CFD (MR-TP)
models.what_it_computes: Transient, pore-scale primary atomization and near-field droplet size spectrum using interface-capturing with surface tension and contact-line physics

models.name: Aerosol Transport and Breakup CFD (ATB)
models.what_it_computes: Far-field aerosol evolution through the plenum and mouthpiece, including secondary breakup, coalescence, evaporation, and transport; outputs droplet size distribution at the mouthpiece exit

mechanisms.name: Primary atomization at the vibrating mesh
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Sets the initial droplet size spectrum emitted from individual orifices, a dominant determinant of delivered dose and regional lung deposition

mechanisms.name: Downstream secondary processes
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Aerodynamic shear, coalescence, and evaporation in the mouthpiece and near-field plume reshape the size distribution prior to inhalation

deviation.detail: Each credibility factor is rated on an Assurance Index from 0 to 12, where higher values indicate stronger evidence

sections: Context of use: Predicting steady-state droplet size distribution at the mouthpiece exit to support design verification and bench-testing reduction
Model risk assessment: Medium risk based on moderate decision consequence (dose accuracy and labeling) and shared evidence with bench tests; model influence is contributory, not exclusive
Device and mechanisms: Vibrating mesh architecture, operating envelope, and mechanistic pathways to droplet size outcomes
Computational models: MR-TP and ATB formulations, domains, and key outputs
Methods: credibility activities limited to Discretization error, Model form, Model inputs, Numerical code verification, Numerical solver error, Output comparison, and Test conditions
Methods: Assurance Index (0–12) rubric and factor-specific evaluation procedures
Results: Model 1 × Mechanism 1 (MR-TP × Primary atomization) — pair summary
Numerical code verification (Assurance Index 8/12) — Model 1 × Mechanism 1
Numerical solver error (Assurance Index 9/12) — Model 1 × Mechanism 1
Results: Model 1 × Mechanism 2 (MR-TP × Downstream secondary processes) — pair summary
Numerical code verification (Assurance Index 7/12) — Model 1 × Mechanism 2
Numerical solver error (Assurance Index 6/12) — Model 1 × Mechanism 2
Results: Model 2 × Mechanism 1 (ATB × Primary atomization) — pair summary
Numerical code verification (Assurance Index 8/12) — Model 2 × Mechanism 1
Numerical solver error (Assurance Index 8/12) — Model 2 × Mechanism 1
Results: Model 2 × Mechanism 2 (ATB × Downstream secondary processes) — pair summary
Numerical code verification (Assurance Index 8/12) — Model 2 × Mechanism 2
Numerical solver error (Assurance Index 9/12) — Model 2 × Mechanism 2
Discussion: Interpretation of factor-specific scores across model–mechanism pairs with emphasis on droplet size distribution fidelity
Limitations and future work: Extending factor coverage and refining inputs without introducing additional credibility dimensions
